title: Characterizing Selective Refusal Bias in Large Language Models
reasoning: The paper includes religion as a core attribute in its bias evaluation. It benchmarks how Large Language Models handle malicious prompts targeting ten different religious and belief groups (Atheist, Bahá'í, Buddhist, Christian, Hindu, Jewish, Mormon, Muslim, Sikh, Taoist), specifically comparing refusal rates and response lengths across these groups to identify safety performance disparities.
